chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Al-Mufazzal ibn Umar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The believers are truly brothers, sons of one father and one mother, and when a vein (of worry/sweat) is struck upon one of them, the others stay awake (in vigil/concern) for him.'

key_terms.بَنُو أَبٍ وَ أُمٍّ: Sons of a father and mother (biological siblings)
key_terms.عِرْقٌ: Vein (metaphor for deep feeling, worry, or sweat of effort)

ai.seo_question: What is the nature of brotherhood among believers according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the bond of faith beyond mere association, defining believers as siblings sharing a single spiritual parentage, which necessitates an active, shared responsibility for one another's well-being. This hadith underscores the Shia concept of *Ukhuwwah* (brotherhood) as a dynamic state of vigilance, where the distress of one member triggers a collective response from the community, reflecting the organic unity of the *Ummah*.
